From 613 to 713: How Previous Year Papers Added 100 Marks

2 min readBeginnerPunjab Police Sub Inspectorprevious year paperspyqpunjab police siexam strategy
Quick answer

I missed the Punjab Police SI cut-off by 10 marks. The next year, I spent the last 3 months only on previous year papers and scored 713. Here is exactly how.

≈ 2 min to finish · Beginner

If you do not study the previous year questions of the exam you are preparing for, clearing it becomes very hard. Let me explain this with my own example.

First attempt: missed by 10 marks

In my first Sub Inspector exam, I scored 613. The general cut-off was 623. I missed the paper by just 10 marks.

The last 3 months: only previous year papers

For the next year's exam, I spent the last 3 months on just one thing: solving previous year papers of Constable, Sub Inspector and Head Constable. My method was:

  1. Solve the paper. The questions I knew were fine.
  2. Search Google for every question I did not know.
  3. If the topic was new to me, study the whole topic from scratch. Search it on Google and make notes on it.

This way, one question covered a whole new topic, and many other questions from that topic got prepared along with it.

The result: 713 marks

In my next SI exam, I scored 713, which is 100 marks more than before. Those 100 marks came from previous year papers.

WhenMy marksResult
First attempt61310 below the cut-off (623)
Next year (last 3 months on previous papers only)713100 marks more

Where to get previous year papers

The Previous Year Questions section on House of Aspirants has the last 10 years' papers of all Punjab government exams, ready to download. Open Previous Year Questions

Straight answers

Frequently asked questions

Are previous year papers enough for Punjab Police SI?

They are the most important part of the last 3 months. I skipped them in my first attempt and missed the cut-off by 10 marks; solving only PYQs in the last 3 months took me from 613 to 713.

How many years of previous papers should I solve?

Solve the last 10 years of papers for your exam and for other Punjab government exams. Questions and patterns repeat more often than most students expect.
